title: Full Voyage
description: Trace one crew member's entire session lifecycle end to end: register, use the access token, refresh it, use the new one, and finally log out — confirming every handoff is clean and nothing from an earlier stage leaks into a later one.
successCondition: Register a new account (201, capture accessToken v1 and the th_refresh cookie). GET /api/auth/me with accessToken v1 returns 200 with matching user data. POST /api/auth/refresh with the cookie returns 200 with a new accessToken v2 and a new th_refresh cookie value (different from v1's cookie). GET /api/auth/me with accessToken v2 returns 200. POST /api/auth/logout with the newest cookie returns 204. A final POST /api/auth/refresh reusing that now-logged-out cookie returns 401.
hints: accessToken v1 doesn't need to be invalidated by the refresh call — access tokens are stateless JWTs valid until they expire on their own; only the refresh token is rotated/revoked.
Capture the Set-Cookie header value explicitly after each call rather than relying on a client's automatic cookie jar, so you can prove the cookie value actually changed between steps.
